## Intent
Hypothesis: fusing the scatter into the auto-vectorized particle update loop eliminates intermediate storage and approaches the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads.

## Cache saturation
Cost FALLS from N=4000 (11.334 ns/p at q=0.01) to N=65000 (7.895) — overhead amortization. Past the L2 spill at N≈60787, cost stays FLAT: 7.803 at N=262000, 7.80 at N=4M, with no knee at the L2→DRAM transition. Death rate raises the floor without changing the N-shape: the plateau moves from 7.80 ns/p (q=0.01) to 8.27 (q=0.05) to 10.49 (q=0.25), flat past N=65000 in every case. The L1d spill at N≈949 is below the smallest measured point.

## Bandwidth
Peak is 8.85 GB/s at N=4M, q=0.01 — 35.1% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling; at q=0.25 it falls to 6.58 GB/s (26.1%). The algo is compute/overhead-bound: ns/p flattens at large N rather than rising toward a DRAM ceiling, and bandwidth plateaus far below the streaming limit. The transition is by death rate, not N — q≤0.05 holds ~8.3 ns/p while q=0.25 rises to ~10.5, cutting bandwidth 25%. It never approaches the streaming ceiling.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized across components of one particle, not across particles. The update loop loads 16 bytes (`ldur q16`) from a single particle, rearranges with `ext.16b` and `mov.s v18[3]`, then applies `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` on four lanes. An indexed `ld1.s {v17}[1]` gathers one component; `fmul.2s`/`fadd.2s` handle the rest. Stride is 0x44 (68 bytes). This component-wise vec explains low bandwidth — 69 bytes touched but compute-heavy per particle. The fused scatter is entirely scalar: 22 `strb` byte stores, 18 `csel` clamps, 6 `ccmp` bounds checks, capping throughput and driving death-rate sensitivity.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 8.85 GB/s (35% of ceiling) at q=0.01, falling to 6.58 GB/s (26%) at q=0.25. Component-wise auto-vectorization (`fmul.4s` on one particle's floats) cannot stream because the compute-to-byte ratio is too high, and the fused scatter's byte-granular `strb` writes with branchy `ccmp`/`csel` dominate as death rate rises. Flat ns/p past the L2 spill (7.80→10.49 ns/p) confirms compute/overhead-bound behavior in every regime.
